newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia seen closer to new pig vaccine.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia seen closer to new pig vaccine.

text.p: A revolutionary Australian pig vaccine had the potential to generate millions of dollars in export earnings, the Minister for Science and Technology Peter McGauran said on Tuesday.

The vaccine, being developed to rid the pig industry of one of its most costly diseases, had moved closer to reality with a A$2.0 million research agreement between the Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation (CSIRO), the Pig Research and Development Corp (PRDC) and the pharmaceutical company Inovax Ltd, he said in a statement.
Inovax will be contributing A$750,000 with the rest provided by the CSIRO and PRDC.
The vaccine technology could eventually be used to treat a wide range of pig diseases, McGauran said.
The focus would be on porcine pleuropneumonia, an often fatal respiratory disease which was recognised as a major problem by pig farmers, he said.
The CSIRO had been developing the genetically-modified live vaccine for three years to offer protection from the disease in a single dose, he said.
With capital and commercial support from Inovax, the treatment should be available within three years, he said.

The new agreement would also enable the CSIRO to further develop the vaccine for other serious pig diseases such as swine fever, porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome and swine dysentery, he said.
